title: Trump Administration Admits It Canceled Clean Energy Grants Only in States That Voted for Harris
excerpt: A court filing reveals the Department of Energy terminated 284 grants in blue states while sparing roughly 340 identical projects in red states from the same cut list.
body:
• A July 15 court filing shows the Department of Energy compiled a list of 624 clean energy grants to cut, then terminated only the 284 in states that voted for Kamala Harris.
  • The remaining 340 grants in Trump-voting states were spared and have not been terminated since.
  • OMB Director Russ Vought had announced the cuts last October, naming 16 blue states affected — totaling nearly $8 billion in canceled funding.
  • Democrats say the filing proves officials "corruptly abused their power" to punish states based on voting patterns.

A Partisan Chopping Block

The Trump administration acknowledged in a federal court filing last week that it selectively terminated clean energy grants based on how states voted in the 2024 presidential election, according to the filing reviewed by the New York Post. The admission came in a case challenging the cancellation of Biden-era clean energy project funding.

""Nearly $8 billion in Green New Scam funding to fuel the Left's climate agenda is being cancelled," Vought wrote."

https://x.com/OccupyDemocrats/status/2080760724432040143

Jeff Novak, the principal deputy general counsel of the Department of Energy, wrote that the agency had initially compiled a list of 624 grants proposed for termination. The White House Office of Management and Budget then whittled that list in half — cutting only those in blue states.

"With one exception, the 284 terminated grants had a recipient location and/or at least one place of performance in a state that awarded its electoral votes to Kamala Harris," Novak stated. The remaining approximately 340 grants in Trump-voting states "were not terminated in October 2025, and they have not since been terminated."

$8 Billion in Canceled Funding

OMB Director Russ Vought announced the cuts on social media last October, specifically naming California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Oregon, Vermont and Washington as affected states. "Nearly $8 billion in Green New Scam funding to fuel the Left's climate agenda is being cancelled," Vought wrote.

Democrats Cry Foul

Democratic lawmakers said the filing demonstrates that Trump administration officials "corruptly abused their power" to terminate grants solely based on the political identity of the states receiving federal money. The admission adds to a growing list of legal challenges accusing the administration of using federal funds as political leverage.

In a separate but related action this week, 25 states and the District of Columbia sued the Trump administration for conditioning FEMA disaster preparedness grants on election-related changes. The Department of Homeland Security had threatened to withhold 20 percent of more than $1 billion in grants unless states switched from electronic voting systems to hand-marked paper ballots.

What It Means for Indian Americans

The terminated grants included clean energy projects in states with large Indian American populations — California, New Jersey, New York, Illinois and Massachusetts among them. The cancellations could affect jobs in renewable energy, a sector that employs a growing number of Indian-origin engineers and entrepreneurs.
